claims: Perp mark-to-market has a checked break-even characterization and two distinct prices separate positions.
Matched long/short base exposure makes funding redistributive: funding payments sum to zero.
Funding is bilinear in the rate and shifts the effective mark price from p to p-r.
Nonzero funding-rate kernel is exactly zero base exposure.
For a list of per-epoch long/short payments, per-epoch budget balance composes into cumulative budget balance.
Across integer funding epochs, the total floor-division rounding gap stays between -N and 0.
The epoch gate composition theorem bundles budget balance, integer gap bounds, conservation, extraction bound, and effective price shift into one system-level witness.
proof_method: integer linear algebra for mark-to-market and funding homomorphisms
reuse of existing funding-rate extraction and integer-gap theorems
record-valued composition of per-epoch safety obligations

boundaries: These are algebraic and epoch-gate composition proofs. They do not prove oracle freshness, clearing-price admissibility, or runtime authorization.
The epoch gate composition reuses existing extraction-bound and integer-gap theorems from PerpFundingRateSafety; it assumes those modeled inputs faithfully represent runtime funding calculations.
The funding conservation theorem applies to matched base exposure; unmatched books require a separate imbalance or insurance accounting proof.
